correctness.rationale: The quoted finite CW action and group generators are explicit. Rank-six EL-shellability yields simply connected covering complex; every reflection fixes a nontrivial proper rank-one noncrossing partition, so Armstrong gives π1=0. Exhaustive full-chain dihedral orbit enumeration has f-vector (47,542,1954,2680,1231) with independent Burnside fixed counts; exact signed boundaries square to zero. 3221 reproducible unimodular chain cancellations leave Z^10 -> Z with gcd 7, giving only H3=Z/7 and H4=Z^9. Simply connectedness and H2=0 give two-connectivity. For a finite two-connected 4-complex, the 3-skeleton is a wedge of S3 and the degree-matrix classification of 4-cell attachments yields M(Z/7,3) ∨ 9 S4. Source and certificate embedded. Finite computation proves only these finite chain facts, not the cited general theorems. An independent seven-local Cartan–Leray and transfer argument recovers the order-seven H3 class from the free sevenfold rotation action and involutive inversion; possible 2-primary torsion and the exact free rank still require the integer certificate.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The published statements imply some ingredients (fixed partitions, covering connectivity, simple connectivity via stabilizers), but not the torsion attaching degree nor nine free four-dimensional spheres. A new exact integer quotient reduction supplies the missing implication. The earlier NC6/C6 calculation concerns a different rank and only rotations; the heptagon D7 quotient additionally folds the free rotation quotient by nonfree reflections, for which neither the integral torsion-free part nor possible 2-primary torsion follows from the hexagon computation. Prime-polygon noncrossing-diagonal complexes are not noncrossing-partition order complexes. The 7-primary H3 class is also predicted by standard cyclic group homology and transfer once freeness is established, so it is not presented alone as a new general theorem; the exact full integral homotopy type, including absence of 2-primary torsion and the nine-sphere rank, is the distinct new result.

value.rationale: The first seven-point prime dihedral noncrossing-partition quotient is a canonical Coxeter-Catalan orbit complex. Computing its complete homotopy type identifies a previously unresolved order-seven attaching map and nine free top spheres, not just f-vectors or rational Betti numbers. Reflection fixed points force simply connectedness while higher torsion survives, a genuine topological distinction from a free cyclic quotient. The exact finite natural object and its complete type are independently motivated by the 2005 dihedral enumeration literature.
